alignments.note: Presentative frame 'it came to pass' with its dummy subject (rule 21). The apodosis opens with its own waw, so that waw and not this verb carries the ASV's 'that' (rule 45), and the verb keeps only 'it came to pass'.
kaʾăšer fused into when (rule 30); head taken on the preposition, though heading on the relative is equally defensible.
Object marker; the ASV writes the object bare (rule 16).

The apodosis opens with this waw, so it carries the frame's 'that' (rule 45). The ASV prints the word ahead of the temporal clause rather than at the apodosis, which makes the unit reordered under rule 25; the competing reading takes that placement as evidence and gives the 'that' to the presentative verb instead, but rule 45 keys the decision to the presence of an apodosis waw, not to position.
Hithpael with its reflexive pronoun and particle; head on the lexical verb (rule 44).
No article morpheme; the noun takes a supplied the (rule 29).
Directive he licenses the English to.

review_notes: Corrected the placement of the ASV's 'that'. The accepted alignment gave it to the presentative wayhî and marked the apodosis waw unrepresented, on the ground that 'no apodosis waw is written for the ASV's that'; but a waw does open the apodosis (s011, וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ), which is exactly rule 45's second case, where the waw carries the 'that' and the verb keeps only 'it came to pass'.

The ASV prints 'that' before the temporal clause ('came to pass, that, when ... heard'), so the corrected unit is reordered relative to the Hebrew; rule 25 allows this, and rule 45 offers position as a consequence rather than as the deciding evidence.

The chapter's other three presentative frames — 24.15, 24.22, 24.30 — all place the 'that' on the apodosis waw, so the corrected reading also matches how the same construction was resolved elsewhere in GEN.24.
